provenance: Computed by the LunarWindow pipeline from NASA LOLA terrain and NASA SPICE (DE421) ephemerides. Code written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and verified by the team with automated tests and a comparison against NASA PGDA illumination maps.
verdict: Touchdown 2028-09-01T01 UTC: the Sun's centre is 1.54 deg above the skyline and the top of Earth's disc 0.00 deg above the skyline (power and a link at landing).
Over 14 days: Sun up 100%, Earth in view 88%, both 88% of the time.
Survives the mission: the battery never drops below 140 Wh (lowest 700 Wh).
No darkness during the mission: no cold soak.
Battery needed: 0 Wh of the 560 Wh it can use above its 140 Wh floor.
Battery model: power = panel power x visible Sun, whatever the Sun's direction (a sun-tracking array), so survival is an upper bound for fixed panels.
why: Marginal touchdown: the top of Earth's disc clears the skyline by under 0.5 deg; Earth is 0.00 deg above the skyline (bearing 162 deg, set by terrain 430 m away at 0.17 deg), so there is almost no margin for a landing error, a lower antenna or a later hour.
Longest Earth blackout from 2028-09-13T08 UTC (41 h): terrain 440 m away blocks it (bearing 150 deg: skyline 0.22 deg, centre of the body at -0.14 deg).
The Sun stays up all mission: its closest pass, 2028-09-14T03 UTC, is 0.40 deg above the skyline (bearing 35 deg, set by terrain 9.6 km away at 1.12 deg).
